title: UK refrigeration flaw: Guardian says a secret NCSC-led operation warded off the risk; LBC reports a race to secure fridges
date_note: Published November 20; the flaw was discovered in October per LBC.
summary: LBC reports experts racing to secure tens of thousands of UK fridges and freezers after a significant flaw was found. The Guardian (via AOL) says a Whitehall and NCSC-led operation warded off the risk of an attack; the flaw was in RDM data managers, found by Omega Solutions. RDM's CEO told the BBC it had deployed first patch releases. Pen Test Partners says many thousands at small stores remain exposed.
plain: The Guardian says a UK government-led operation warded off a possible attack on fridge controllers; Pen Test Partners says many thousands at small stores are still exposed.
exec: Pen Test Partners says many thousands of controllers at small stores are still exposed; RDM's CEO says first patch releases were deployed.
action: Small operators: per Pen Test Partners as reported by the Guardian, take refrigeration controllers off the public internet or apply the updated firmware.

validation.note: LBC and the Guardian (read via its AOL copy; the Guardian page itself could not be fetched) both report the flaw, Omega and Pen Test Partners. RDM did not respond to the Guardian per its article. The Guardian says the UK story was first reported by the BBC.

review.note: RDM patch claim was the CEO's statement to the BBC about first patch releases; summary and exec now say so. Rest matches LBC and Guardian.
